title: Read fixed length file with batches
question:
I have a text file with fixed length format like below -

K57 details 1234
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  0123456789
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  0123456789
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  0123456789
K57 details 5678
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  9876543210
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  9876543210
K58 abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz  9876543210
.....
.....

Here K57 is header record of each batch and K58 records are detail records of the batch. There can be multiple batches each having its header(K57) record followed by multiple detail(K58) records.

I need to extract values from each K58 record along with its header record detail in following format -

+----------+------------+------------+
|K57_detail|K58_detail_1|K58_detail_2|
+----------+------------+------------+
|1234      |abcdef      |01234       |
|1234      |abcdef      |01234       |
|1234      |abcdef      |01234       |
|5678      |abcdef      |98765       |
|5678      |abcdef      |98765       |
|5678      |abcdef      |98765       |
+----------+------------+------------+

I know Pyspark substring() function which can help to extract required value from each row. But my real challenge is to bring info of header K57 record to each of its detail records. Any help to achieve the above result will be appreciated. Thanks in advance.
answer:
I would hope for more concrete example in the question but nevertheless;

Here is an example of how you might read fixed length data from a file

data.txt

John      Smith     19851231M12345
Jane      Doe       19900715F67890
Alice     Johnson   19830305F13579

Reading it:

def parse_fixed_length_file(file_path):
    records = []
    with open(file_path, 'r') as file:
        for line in file:
            record = {
                "first_name": line[0:10].strip(),
                "last_name": line[10:20].strip(),
                "dob": line[20:28],
                "gender": line[28],
                "id": line[29:34].strip()
            }
            records.append(record)
    return records

# Example usage
file_path = "data.txt"
parsed_data = parse_fixed_length_file(file_path)
for record in parsed_data:
    print(record)

You can then further process the list of dicts into a dataframe as needed. You will also need to add a check into the for line in file loop to begin collecting a record when a suitable header is found.
